_comment: D3 — plugin overlap map. Rule 9: which plugins claim the same job is
editorial judgement about the WordPress ecosystem, not logic, and it will
need updating as plugins come and go. Keyed by the plugin's directory slug
An overlap is two ACTIVE plugins owning the same responsibility. It is not
automatically a defect — the report says 'pick one owner', not 'delete this'.

image_compression.label: Image compression
image_compression.why_one_owner: Two compressors re-process each other's output, which degrades image quality with no size benefit and makes the result impossible to reason about.

lazy_loading.label: Lazy loading
lazy_loading.why_one_owner: Two lazy-loaders fight over the same images and commonly break the largest one in the first screenful, which is exactly the element Core Web Vitals measures.

page_caching.label: Page caching
page_caching.why_one_owner: Two caches serve each other stale pages and make every cache-clear unreliable.

seo_titles_and_schema.label: SEO titles, meta and schema
seo_titles_and_schema.why_one_owner: Two SEO plugins emit competing title tags and duplicate schema graphs, so search engines see conflicting claims about the same page.

xml_sitemaps.label: XML sitemaps
xml_sitemaps.why_one_owner: Two sitemap generators publish different URL sets, and search engines have no way to know which one you meant.

redirects.label: Redirect management
redirects.why_one_owner: Two redirect engines produce chains and loops that are very hard to trace.

backups.label: Backups
backups.why_one_owner: Two backup plugins double storage cost and make the recovery path ambiguous at the moment you most need it to be obvious.

families._comment: Free/premium pairs of the SAME product. Never an overlap — flagging a plugin against its own add-on is noise (P7).
